request.spec:
A button downloads the people of the whole tree as a CSV file: a header line
sheet,name,grade,due-total then one line per person, this sheet first in list order, then the
other sheets of the tree by sheet id.
request.prompt:

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button downloads the people of the whole tree as a CSV file: a header line

agent.result_text:
I added an "Export tree people (CSV)" button (`data-testid="export-tree"`), and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**What it does:** pressing the button downloads `tree-<sheet>.csv`. The first line is the header `sheet,name,grade,due-total`. Then come this sheet's people in list order, followed by the people of the other sheets in the tree, sorted by sheet id.

**What counts as "the tree":** I used the app's existing definition — the sheet's parent chain plus all of its children, their children, and so on. Sibling sheets (other children of the same parent) are not included. The app already had a `GET /api/sheets/{id}/tree` endpoint that returns those ids, so I made no server or database changes.

**How values are worked out:**
- **Grade and due-total:** each person's grade is the one in force on their own sheet's today, and their due-total is shown the way their own sheet shows it, including `n/a`.
- **Freshness:** every sheet is re-read from the store when the button is pressed. If the screen is set to an as-of date, the figures are as of that date, the same as the existing people export.
- **CSV formatting:** quoting works the same way as the existing people export.

The change is one new front-end file, `src/main/frontend/features/people/treeexport.slot.tsx`. It reuses the people export's CSV quoting and the existing due and grade calculations.
